create.name: Vidyamala Burch
create.bio:
Vidyamala Burch is a New Zealand-born mindfulness and compassion teacher, ordained in the Triratna Buddhist Order in 1995, whose Buddhist name means 'garland of wisdom'. Spinal injuries at seventeen left her with lasting pain and partial paralysis, and meditation became her way of easing the mental anguish that came with it. Out of that practice she shaped a mindfulness-based approach to living with pain and difficulty, and in 2001 she co-founded Breathworks with Gary Hennessey and Sona Fricker; it now trains teachers in dozens of countries. She was appointed OBE in 2022.

Her teaching blends secular mindfulness with the Buddhist themes of impermanence, acceptance and connection, summed up in her six-step BE AWARE path: be present, accept, wake up to wonder, notice arising and passing, relate to others, and engage with life. Each Tuesday evening, UK time, she leads a free half-hour meditation on Zoom and YouTube, and she teaches online courses, workshops and talks for organisations, and coaches individuals. Her books include Living Well with Pain and Illness, Mindfulness for Health with Danny Penman, published in the US as You Are Not Your Pain, and Mindfulness for Women.

books.title: Living Well with Pain and Illness
books.author: Vidyamala Burch
books.description: Her first book, on finding a different relationship with physical pain through mindfulness, with meditations and everyday suggestions drawn from her own years of living with injury.

courses.title: Freeing the Mind When the Body Hurts
courses.description: A self-paced video course made with Tricycle magazine, in six units that follow her BE AWARE steps, mixing teaching, meditation and contemplative exercises rooted in Buddhist ideas of impermanence and connection.

free_resources.title: Free weekly meditations
free_resources.description: A free half-hour guided meditation every Tuesday at 7pm UK time, open on Zoom or as a YouTube live stream with no sign-up.
